ledger.note: 1343: Veera Ballala III is killed. 'Veera Ballala III was killed at the battle of Madurai in 1343' (the Veera Ballala III page puts his death at Kannanur, infobox 8 September 1342).

region.text: the Hoysala realm of 1343, merged with the areas of Harihara I

ledger.note: 1343: the Hoysala kingdom ends. 'the sovereign territories of the Hoysala Kingdom were merged with the areas administered by Harihara I' in the Tungabhadra region; Harihara I and Bukka Raya I 'had served the king in a military capacity' (Veera Ballala III page); the queen's grant of 1346 is on the same day as Harihara's.

wars.name: Hoysala-Chola war for Gangavadi
wars.outcome: Vishnuvardhana defeats the Chola general Adiyamma near Talakadu in 1116, recovers Gangavadi and chases the Cholas to Vellore.
wars.note: The page gives the 1116 date for the victory only; the Chola raids on Talakadu and the pursuit to Vellore are undated. The Chola dossier puts the loss of the Gangavadi districts 'around 1118' on other pages.

wars.name: Vishnuvardhana's wars with the Western Chalukyas

zones.text: Banavasi, Hanagal, Uchchangi, Bankapura and Lakkundi

wars.outcome: The Hoysalas take Banavasi and Humacha after Hallur (c. 1120), reach the Krishna by c. 1122, accept Chalukya subordination after Achugi's victory, and recapture Hanagal, Uchchangi and Bankapura c. 1140.
wars.note: Majumdar says Vishnuvardhana still held the Krishna region c. 1131 (page); the dates are c. throughout.

wars.name: Ballala II's northern wars

zones.text: Hangal, Belvola, Banavasi, Soratur and Lakkundi

wars.outcome: Hangal annexed c. 1178, seized by the Kalachuri commander Sankama c. 1179 and the invasion ends in a truce, Banavasi retaken from the exiled Someshvara VI by c. 1190, Bhillama V beaten at Soratur and Lakkundi c. 1191, and Ballala II 'emperor over the entire modern Karnataka region' by c. 1192.

wars.name: Yadava reconquest north of the Tungabhadra

zones.text: the Karnataka land between the Tungabhadra and the Krishna ('all these territories north of the Tungabhadra River'); the polygon approximates the river

wars.outcome: 'After c. 1212, he lost all these territories north of the Tungabhadra River to Yadava king Singhana II.'

wars.name: Hoysala intervention in the Chola-Pandya war
wars.outcome: Prince Narasimha II repulses the Pandyas and restores Kulothunga III; the Hoysalas gain a hegemony over the Chola and Pandya kingdoms (1220-1245).
wars.note: Around c. 1216 Maravarman Sundara Pandya ascended the throne at Madurai; the Hoysala page dates the defeat of the Pandyas to 1217.

wars.name: Hoysala-Pandya war under Vira Someshwara
wars.outcome: Vira Someshwara 'stayed back at Kannanur with Ramanatha where he was killed in a war with' Sadayavarman Sundara Pandyan I; the Tamil holdings are lost 'during a Pandya uprising' and recaptured by Veera Ballala III toward the end of the 13th century.
wars.note: The pages give no year for the war, the uprising or the recapture; 1262-1263, 1263 and c. 1295 are bridges (confidence 1).

wars.name: Delhi Sultanate invasions of the Hoysalas
wars.outcome: Halebidu is sacked on 26 February 1311 and again c. 1327; the Hoysalas pay tribute, retreat to Tiruvannamalai and are broken by the Madurai Sultanate; Veera Ballala III dies in 1342-3 and the realm merges with Harihara I's lands. The tribute to Delhi runs 1311 to c. 1318 (ledger vassal events).
wars.note: 1342 (Veera Ballala III infobox, death 8 September 1342 at Kannanur) against 1343 (Hoysala page, battle of Madurai): 1343 is used for the end.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary or a treaty line; the northern marches (Banavasi, Hangal, Lakkundi, the Krishna) changed hands with every war, and the Tamil holdings are circles round Kannanur.

sources.title: Hoysala Empire
sources.note: Identity, infobox capitals and dynastic span (950-1346), dated sentences 1116, 1193, 1217, 1220-1245, c. 1225, 1311, 1318, 1336, 1343, 1346; no area in km2. Cliopatria's title is 'Hoysala Kingdom'; the article opened is the 'Hoysala Empire' page. Re-read 2026-10-19: feudatories of the Western Chalukyas, Tamil territory 'lost during a Pandya uprising' and recaptured, no 1254 division.

sources.title: Vishnuvardhana
sources.note: Campaigns c. 1117-c. 1140 and the c. 1152 death; Gangavadi, Banavasi, Hanagal, Lakkundi. Re-read: c.1122 subordination, Banavasi and Humacha, no loss of Banavasi after 1122.

sources.title: Veera Ballala II
sources.note: Reign from 22 July 1173; Hangal c. 1178, the Kalachuri truce c. 1179, Banavasi c. 1190, Soratur c. 1191, the realm c. 1192 and the loss north of the Tungabhadra after c. 1212. Re-read: Sankama seized Hangal c. 1179, Someshvara VI at Banavasi, Karnataka emperor c. 1192, 'nominal subordination' to the Kalachuris.

sources.title: Veera Ballala III
sources.note: Reign 1292-1342; 26 February 1311 sack of Halebidu, the second sack c. 1327, Tiruvannamalai, the war at Kannanur c. 1342-3, Harihara and Bukka. Re-read: tribute and Veera Virupaksha at Delhi (1311), refusal after 1318.

sources.title: Vira Someshwara
sources.note: Reign 1234-1263; Magadai Mandalam 1236, Kannanur capital after 1235, the 1254 division between Ramanatha and Narasimha III, death at Kannanur. Re-read: 1254 division, killed at Kannanur in the war with Sundara Pandyan I (no year).

notes:
WHAT THE ROW IS. Cliopatria's Hoysala shapes are a core of 441 cells (111,000 km2) on the Mysore plateau and the Malnad (Karnataka 393, Andhra Pradesh 25, Kerala 12, Tamil Nadu 10), 1111-1351. The pages give a larger realm in two spells and a longer life at both ends. START/END: Cliopatria 1111-1351; the pages give Vishnuvardhana's reign from c. 1108 (state drawn from 1108 on the 1111 outline) and the end in 1343 (Veera Ballala III killed; territories merged with Harihara I's; infobox 1342 for his death; dynastic span 950-1346 and the 1346 grant on the same day as Harihara's), so the 1344 shape is marked wrong and belongs to Vijayanagara, whose own 1344 shape has no cell in common with it.

NORTHERN MARCHES (Banavasi, Hangal, Hanagal, Uchchangi, Bankapura, Lakkundi and 'the entire modern Karnataka region' to the Malaprabha and Krishna c. 1192-c. 1212) are in no Cliopatria shape; they are ledger gains and losses on the core, with a polygon approximating the Krishna (16.4 N) and the Tungabhadra (15.0 N at the west). The page dates are 'c.' and the Hangal statements contradict each other (annexed c. 1178 versus seized by the Kalachuri commander c. 1179).

1250-1325: Cliopatria removes the southern half (Mysuru, Hassan, Talakadu, Hosur) and keeps the Halebidu half, and brings it back in 1326. The Vira Someshwara page divides the kingdom in 1254 between Ramanatha (Kannanur, in the Tamil country) and Narasimha III (Halebidu); the Hoysala page has the Hoysala kingdom whole until 1343. Cliopatria's treatment is not on any page, so the three shapes are corrected to the 1241 outline. The Tamil holdings (Kannanur Kuppam c. 1225, Magadai Mandalam 1236, the 1254 southern branch, the c. 1295 recovery) are circles round Tiruchirappalli (confidence 1-2); Magadai Mandalam is not located on the page.

VASSALAGE. The Western Chalukya dossier records the Hoysalas as Chalukya vassals from c. 1122 (their page: Vishnuvardhana 'accepted Chalukya subordination'); the tribute to the Delhi Sultan after 1311 is the Khalji dossier's vassal event. The 1220-1245 client tint over the Chola and Pandya shapes is my reading of 'hegemony' (confidence 2).

NOT SETTLED (page budget of 5 spent): the Pandya uprising that cost the Tamil land and its date; whether Narasimha III's northern branch lost anything 1254-1292; the Tughluq campaign's year (c. 1327); Ballala III's Pandya intervention c. 1310; any area figure (the infobox gives none; text: 'most of present-day Karnataka plus parts of Tamil Nadu and southwestern Telangana', ratio of the Cliopatria core to modern Karnataka about 0.57); the ruler strip (the pages give only some reigns, so none is written). Counterparts without dossiers: Kalachuri of Kalyani, Madurai Sultanate (established c. 1335-6), the Sinda chief Achugi. Gazetteer names needed: Halebidu, Talakadu, Banavasi, Hangal, Lakkundi, Kannanur Kuppam, Srirangam, Magadai Mandalam, Gangavadi, Soratur.

REPAIR OF 2026-10-19 (reviewer findings; all five pages re-read). (1) Keyframes: 1126, 1188 and 1241 were marked ok but did not hold the land the ledger gains. They are now adjust, with new keyframes 1120, 1140, 1179, 1192, 1212, 1225, 1236, 1263 and 1295 so that every gain and loss of the ledger shows (Banavasi and Humacha 1120, the marches to Lakkundi 1140, Hangal out 1179, Karnataka south of the Krishna 1192, the Yadava loss north of the Tungabhadra 1212, the Tamil holdings 1225/1236, lost 1263 and recaptured c. 1295). The 1241 union is 626 cells against the reviewer's 626 (439 in Cliopatria's shape; 72 between it and the Tungabhadra, 118 Tamil). 1250, 1260 and 1285 now restore that union, not the bare 1241 outline; 1326 and 1333 add the same land. (2) Vassal events: Western Chalukyas 1122-1126 (mirroring western-chalukya-empire /ledger/25-26) and Delhi 1311-c. 1318, both from the vassal's side. (3) Counterparts: 1190 is the exiled Chalukya rump of Someshvara VI (page: 'Someshvara VI'); 1192 is yadava-dynasty. (4) Hangal: loss c. 1179 to the Kalachuris; its recovery is not on the page, so the c. 1192 event covers it. (5) Pandya war: contest 1262-1263, loss of the Tamil holdings 1263 and recapture c. 1295, all bridges at confidence 1; the 1254 division and 1295 merge were dropped (two kings of one state, Ramanatha at Kannanur and Narasimha III at Halebidu, which the Hoysala Empire page does not mention at all). (6) Not done (thin): a ruler strip; the 1254 border. Mirrors for other authors: western-chalukya-empire has no loss of Banavasi/Humacha (1120) or Hanagal/Uchchangi/Bankapura (1140) and nothing for the Someshvara VI rump after 1187; chola-empire has no Hoysala vassal 1220-1245 and no 1225/1236 losses; yadava-dynasty should mirror the 1192 loss and 1212 gain; pandya-empire the 1263 gain and c. 1295 loss; khalji-dynasty the 1311 vassal. No disagreement with the review beyond the choices above.
